title: Cadbury Celebrations Turns Diwali Gifting Toward the Neighbour You Bicker With
excerpt: Mondelez India's 2026 Diwali campaign, built around the short film 'The Neighbour,' recasts festive gifting as a peace offering — and launches Milky Mithai Squares, a chocolate built on the flavours of Indian mithai.
body:
• Cadbury Celebrations' Diwali 2026 campaign centres on neighbours: the parking-spot, boundary-wall, noisy-party frictions of close-quarters living, and the festival as the moment to reset them.
  • The campaign film, 'The Neighbour,' frames a box of Celebrations as the gesture that turns everyday nok-jhok — affectionate bickering — into, in the campaign's phrase, a little love.
  • Mondelez India is using the campaign to launch Milky Mithai under the Celebrations brand: chocolate made with slow-cooked, caramelised milk in the flavours of traditional Indian mithai.
  • The brand has also refreshed its festive gifting range with new pack formats and designs for the season.

The Diwali ad aimed at the people closest to home

Most Diwali advertising aims at family. Cadbury Celebrations' 2026 campaign, launched October 12 in Mumbai, aims one door closer: the neighbours. Mondelez India's festive push for its flagship gifting brand is built on the small frictions of residential life in India — the disputed parking spot, the shared boundary wall, the pet, the late-night party, the compound cricket game — and on Diwali as the natural moment to set them aside.

The campaign's short film, titled 'The Neighbour,' dramatises that arc: everyday bickering, then a box of chocolates as the peace offering. The brand's framing is that the tiffs and the affection are the same relationship — neighbours are among the most constant people in our lives, and the festival gives the friction a reset button.

"We bicker, we banter but underneath, there is bonhomie, especially during Diwali."

— Vinay Subramanyam, Vice President – Marketing, Mondelez India

A mithai-chocolate hybrid leads the product push

The campaign doubles as a product launch. Under the Celebrations brand, Mondelez is introducing Milky Mithai — billed as a coming together of chocolate with the taste of traditional Indian mithai, made with slow-cooked, golden caramelised milk, in a special Mithai collection gift box for the festival. The wider Celebrations gifting range gets new pack formats and designs for the season, aimed at the corporate and family gifting market that peaks in the fortnight before Diwali.

The strategy is legible: branded chocolate has spent decades trying to displace the mithai box as India's default festive gift, and a chocolate that claims mithai's flavours is the most direct attempt yet to merge the two. Whether it lands will be visible in the season's sales — but the cultural observation underneath the campaign is sound, and it is the one diaspora families will recognise first: at Diwali, the sweet box is rarely about the sweets. It is the excuse to knock on a door. The campaign details are at Business Briefing Today.
